condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

- Develop an anticorruption operational framework for MoSS that ensures better governance, hierarchy, reporting and accountability mechanisms and reduced corruption and manipulation routes for service provision departments - Conduct impact evaluation review on social protection issues covered by MOSS Waai program to measure social and behaviour change among marginalized groups targeted by MOSS through the national center for social and criminology studies - Develop and disseminate key messages among the youths to safeguard and protect the elderly in their families and communities from contracting Covid-19 through social-media and media campaigns (TV and radio) - Utilize existing Waai’s Good Hygiene Practices pillar to combat the spread of Covid-19, and promoting social distancing as a protective measure, and correcting wrongful Covid-19 related misinformation and rumors, as well as Waai’s Economic Empowerment pillar for those financially impacted by Covid-19 through social-media and media campaigns (TV and radio) - Finalize and launch community outreach national operational framework for enhancing community mobilization and awareness systems targeting MoSS beneficiaries

- Printing of 1000 copies (first edition) of Waai Training Manual including messages of 12 issues, positive stories from the ground, and communication tools targeting MoSS Social Workers (2300 workers to be expanded) including Community Raedat, Education Facilitators, and NGOs field teams. - 600 copies of manual disseminated to community schools’ facilitators to incorporate Waai messages within the scope of activities and education communication extracurricular materials targeting facilitators as a preliminary step and furthermore, students and parents targeted in the community schools. - Printing of 2400 copies (100 copies each of waai booklet) for disseminating in Minya and Aswan governorates (Community Raedat in both governorates and for dissemination to respective CDAs supporting MoSS in expanding advocacy and awareness messages on 12 social issues included in program). - Detailed workplan for step down training in 27 governorates included in the comprehensive training plan developed for training social teams and workers of MoSS in collaboration with the Women’s General Department and Social Solidarity Directorates of the 27 governorates. Implementation starts simultaneously after completion of each TOT workshop. - Dissemination of Waai Training Manual to master trainers (printed copies of manual + presentations of trainers on waai flasher in printed waai file with the unified design of the program). - A study was initially supported by UNDP designed an anticorruption operational framework with recommendations on improving and strengthening monitoring and accountability mechanisms at MoSS (cash transfer and social care programs). This study set the groundwork for future activities supported by UK Government. - Contracting National Center for Social and Criminological Studies (NCSCR) to develop a national observatory for socio-behavioral change and a national database for informal sector workers - Consultation meetings took place with the NCSCR to develop a conceptual action plan for implementation of signed contract to consolidate a national social observatory for socio-economic behaviors and a national database for informal sector workers - Launch of MoSS social media and on-ground campaign on child marriage detrimants under the slogan “Her Marriage Before The Age Of 18 Deprives Her Of Her Rights”with an aggregate outreach of approximately 32.5 million beneficiaries. The campaign caters to support national policies condemning child marriage as a practice that violates the rights of the girl child. - National Policies supported include the issuance of a law to criminalize all forms of marriage under 18 years and furthermore, the social protection schemes of MoSS to mainstream the prevention of child marriage among the conditionalities of Takaful Program. (Child Marriage Campaign activities are co-funded with UK government)
- The rest of the planned activities were brought to halt due to delays in recieving the remaining UK tranches

- Information, education and communication (IE&C) material and training manuals on Waai developed - 4,000 Social Workers and Public Service workers are successfully trained on Step Down training - The Policy Resource Group (technical advocacy experts and development experts on Waai component) is in place - Media campaigns on “Waai” program curricula are implemented in targeted local communities - An anticorruption operational framework for MoSS that ensures better governance, hierarchy, reporting and accountability mechanisms and reduced corruption and manipulation routes for service provision departments, is in place

• Waai Comprehensive Manual covering 12 key Waai messages has developed, designed and printed to be used by social workers (Raedat), MoSS personnel, communication experts, NGO personnel etc. • Child marriage booklet had been developed, designed and disseminated in Waai campaigns in 4 governorates in Upper Egypt as part of a national campaign under the auspices of the Minister of Social Solidarity. • Waai youth awareness sessions were organized in Al Asmarat center to mobilize young, contribute to the advocacy of Waai issues and linking them to the services provided by MoSS. A total of Twelve awareness sessions were organized in seven nurseries reached 2,100 persons including nursery personnel and NGO personnel managing the nurseries • Manual for Training of Trainers (TOT) and stepdown training of Social Workers (Ra’edat) was developed including the pre- and post- assessment of trainers. • Operational Manual for the role of Social Workers (Ra’edat) including their selection criteria and monitoring and evaluation framework was developed to support recruiting more social workers and expanding their number from 2,500 to 20,000 persons • Two Field visits were implemented in Cairo (Al Asmarat) with selected journalists to raise awareness on Positive Parenting and FGM Abandonment which was followed by media coverage on media profile executed with national and private newspaper websites including – Youm 7 – Ahram – Masrawy – Al Watan News – Al Dostor – 8 TV and Radio Programs (DMC + CBC Extra News + Radio Networks) • A 16 Days of Activism social media campaign- co-funded by the Government of the United Kingdom and the European Union- reached around 8 million persons and the official page of the Ministry of Solidarity received more than 380,000 interactions, 8,500 comments, and more than 500,000 views of the campaigns videos. Additionally, on-the ground awareness activities by Ra’edat reached more than 100,000 beneficiaries. • The operational framework for Waai interventions had been completed by Waai experts focusing on the 52 districts targeted by the Presidential Initiative Hayah Karema (Decent life). The Framework includes direct MoSS interventions, and partners activities by contracted or selected NGOs as well as partnerships with relevant national stakeholders such as the Ministries of Culture, Youth and Sports, and Information etc. • Around 4,000 Face Masks were delivered to North-Sinai as emergency intervention, in cooperation with Red Crescent Association, with hygiene practices messages and other Waai messages related to civil rights, education and girls rights (early marriage and FGM abandonment). The Face Masks were distributed via 2 Medical Convoys held and 2,000 masks were distributed per convoy. • A new organogram have been developed, reviewed and approved by the central agency for organization and administration (CAOA) to accommodate the required restructuring of MoSS Departments, strengthen the quality of services delivered to the public and enhance expansion of programs related to economic empowerment of vulnerable groups, social protection, social care, and effective engagement of civil society in social development schemes. • A study including an anticorruption operational framework was delivered with recommendations on improving and strengthening monitoring and accountability mechanisms at MoSS (cash transfer and social care programs). • Completed 105 trainings for 3,000 participants in leadership, Customer service and complaints management, projects management, design thinking, digital transformation, code of conduct and Governance. There is an ongoing collaboration with the central department for information systems and digital transformation to work on a platform for the ministry to disseminate digital training programs and to work on the e-archiving process of the training programs.

comment.narrative: A newly developed organizational structure of MoSS departments, accredited by CAOA, is operationalized, to enhance public service delivery. Organizational structures of MoSS departments providing services directly to the public or indirectly through supervising NGOS' operation of MoSS institutions are mapped. Additionally, a total of around 100 training sessions for participants consisting of heads and employees from the Ministry of Social Solidarity's central and technical departments, including social protection, social care, development, and Civil Society Affairs, across the 27 governorates, are conducted.

A new organogram for MoSS, accredited by the Central Authority for Organization and Administration (CAOA) has bee developed and is operationalized, to enhance public service delivery. Organizational structure of MoSS departments providing services directly to the public or indirectly, has been mapped. Additionally, a draft organizational structure for the National Council for PwDs was developed. A total of 157 training sessions for 4,370 participants consisting of heads and employees from central and technical departments, including social protection, social care, development, and Civil Society Affairs, across 27 governorates, have been implemented. The training programs encompassed a range of topics such as leadership, customer service and complaints management, project management, design thinking, digital transformation, code of conduct, and governance.

A significant number of Waai packages have been printed and disseminated to support the implementation of on-ground awareness activities and campaigns of the Waai Programme. These packages comprise 12 Waai booklets covering the 12 pertinent issues and have been distributed among community social workers, MoSS directorates, partner NGOs, and the media. The includes developing and printing of 2400 copies (100 copies each of the Waai booklet) in Minya and Aswan governorates. Furthermore, 3000 packages of Waai booklets have been printed to support the Child Marriage campaign field activities carried out by social workers, MoSS directorates, MoSS partners from contracted NGOs, and the media. Additionally, 8000 Waai booklets for family planning and Maternal Child Health were designed and printed, along with 1000 copies of leaflets containing the 12 messages of the Waai Programme.

Religious leaders and representatives from various religious institutions including Dar Al-Iftah, Ministry of Endowments, and three Egyptian churches, receive training aimed at developing religious leaders' understanding and adoption of Waai Programme's social development issues. Additionally, a forum is launched, including religious leaders and representatives from Islamic and Christian religious institutions to present policy/media briefs for the dissemination of their respective Waai Programme messages.

Two training sessions were conducted for 75 religious leaders from various institutions, including Dar Al-Iftah, Al-Azhar, Ministry of Endowments, and three Egyptian churches (Catholic, Coptic Orthodox, and Coptic Evangelical church). The training set the foundation for the launch and implementation of the forum, titled "Dialogue Platform on the Integration of the Roles of Religious and Social Institutions in Shaping Social Awareness," in Cairo.
